nodes.summary: The first-order (tangent-line) characterization of a convex differentiable function: the graph lies above every tangent line.
nodes.title: Convex differentiable functions lie above their tangent lines

nodes.summary: Eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite symmetric operator are nonnegative: an eigenvalue is the Rayleigh quotient at a unit eigenvector.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite operator are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Eigenvalues of a positive definite symmetric operator are positive.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a positive definite operator are positive

nodes.summary: The entropy tangent bound in an arbitrary orthonormal basis. Its diagonal entries need not align with the eigenvalues of `S`; `klein_entropy` supplies the aligned quantum-relative-entropy form.
nodes.title: Entropy tangent bound in an arbitrary orthonormal basis

nodes.summary: Klein's entropy inequality in the eigenbasis of `S`. The eigenvalue at index `i` is paired with its eigenvector, so this is the quantum-relative-entropy form up to the trace terms. In particular, its tangent correction vanishes when `T = S`.
nodes.title: Klein's entropy inequality

nodes.summary: Klein's inequality (sum form): for a convex function `f` differentiable at the eigenvalues of `S`, the tangent-line sum at the eigenvalues of `S` evaluated on the diagonal of `T` is at most the sum of `f` over the eigenvalues of `T`.
nodes.title: Klein's inequality
Klein's inequality for the square function

nodes.summary: Peierls' inequality for the exponential function.
nodes.title: Peierls' inequality for the exponential

nodes.summary: The diagonal of a self-adjoint operator in any orthonormal basis is majorized by its eigenvalues, as measured by any convex function.
nodes.title: Peierls' inequality

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
